arxiv-1909-07232.title: Improved estimation via model selection method for semimartingale regressions based on discrete data Journal: Journal of Multivariate Analysis
arxiv-1909-07232.creator: Evgeny Pchelintsev, Serguei Pergamenshchikov, Maria Povzun
arxiv-1909-07232.description: Abstract In this paper we study a high dimension (Big Data) semimartingale regression model observed in the discrete time moments. We study this model in a nonparametric setting. To this end improved (shrinkage) estimation methods are developed and the non-asymptotic comparison between shrinkage and least squares estimates are studied.

arxiv-2203-11118.title: Performance Comparisons of Self-stabilizing Algorithms for Maximal Independent Sets
arxiv-2203-11118.creator: Barton F. Cone 1 , Stephen T. Hedetniemi 2 , Lance C. Ingle 3 , Ken Kennedy 1
arxiv-2203-11118.description: Abstract Sensor networks, such as ultra-wideband sensors for the smart warehouse, may need to run distributed algorithms for automatically determining a topological layout. In this paper, we present 5 different self-stabilizing algorithms (their central and distributed counterparts) for determining maximal independent sets.

arxiv-2205-05416.title: Evidence estimation in finite and infinite mixture models and applications
arxiv-2205-05416.creator: Adrien Hairault, Christian P. Robert, Judith Rousseau
arxiv-2205-05416.description: Abstract Estimating the model evidence - or mariginal likelihood of the data - is a notoriously difficult task for finite and infinite mixture models and we reexamine here different Monte Carlo techniques advocated in the recent literature, as well as novel approaches based on Geyer 1994 reverse logistic regression technique, Chib 1995 algorithm, and Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC).

arxiv-2312-08245.title: Combinatorial Stationary Prophet Inequalities
arxiv-2312-08245.creator: Neel Patel, David Wajc
arxiv-2312-08245.description: Abstract Numerous recent papers have studied the tension between thickening and clearing a market in (uncertain, online) long-time horizon Markovian settings. In particular, (Aouad and Saritaç EC’20, Collina et al. WINE’20, Kessel et al. EC’22) studied what the latter referred to as the Stationary Prophet Inequality Problem, due to its similarity to the classic finite-time horizon prophet inequality problem.

arxiv-2404-12914.title: Reduced cross-section in Electron-Ion Colliders at small x x
arxiv-2404-12914.creator: G.R.Boroun, B.Rezaei
arxiv-2404-12914.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by G.R.Boroun, B.Rezaei. The nuclear reduced cross section σ r A \sigma^{A}_{r} , in the kinematic range of the electron-Ion collider with center-of-mass energy s = 140 ​ GeV \sqrt{s}=140~\mathrm{GeV} and y ≤ 1 y{\leq}1 , is discussed. The importance of the nuclear longitudinal structure function F L A F^{A}_{L} and its behavior owing to the impact parameter for the heavy and light nucleus of Pb-208 and C-12 at Q 2 = 5 Q^{2}=5 and 10 ​ GeV 2 10~\mathrm{GeV}^{2} is considered.

arxiv-2509-26427.title: Ascent Fails to Forget
arxiv-2509-26427.creator: Ioannis Mavrothalassitis, Pol Puigdemont, Noam Itzhak Levi, Volkan Cevher
arxiv-2509-26427.description: Abstract Contrary to common belief, we show that gradient ascent-based unconstrained optimization methods frequently fail to perform machine unlearning, a phenomenon we attribute to the inherent statistical dependence between the forget and retain data sets. This dependence, which can manifest itself even as simple correlations, undermines the misconception that these sets can be independently manipulated during unlearning.

pmc-10731633.title: A High-Throughput Experimental Approach to Screening Gas Sorption by Liquids and Solids
pmc-10731633.creator: J Mark Young, Sam H McCalmont, Sophie Fourmentin, Panagiotis Manesiotis, John D Holbrey, Leila Moura
pmc-10731633.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). High-precision measurement of gas uptake from single or mixed feeds in solid and liquid sorbents traditionally requires time-consuming experimental procedures and/or complex and costly equipment. A simple and cost-effective headspace gas chromatography (HS-GC) approach for the fast, universal experimental screening of sorbents for gas uptake and/or determination of their real gas separation selectivity has been developed and is demonstrated for pressures up to 2500 mbar and temperatures above 30 °C.

pmc-10735596.title: STATE-LEVEL EDUCATION CONTEXT AS A MODERATOR OF GENETIC RISK FOR POOR COGNITIVE FUNCTION ACROSS GENDER AND COHORT
pmc-10735596.creator: Eleanor Kerr, Pamela Herd, Katrina Walsemann
pmc-10735596.description: APOE, specifically the e4 allele, is the strongest known genetic risk factor for late-onset dementia. Individuals with at least one copy of the e4 allele have a 3-15 times higher risk for dementia, and faster rates of cognitive decline, than those without it. Although education has been shown to moderate this relationship, the quality of U.S.

pmc-11436702.title: Elevated α-1,2-mannosidase MAN1C1 in glioma stem cells and its implications for immunological changes and prognosis in glioma patients
pmc-11436702.creator: Don Carlo Batara, Hyun-Jin Kim, Le Thi Phan, Minseo Kim, Young-Ok Son, Seongsoo Lee, Sang-Ik Park, Young Sun Choi, Samuel Beck, Sung-Hak Kim
pmc-11436702.description: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is the most aggressive type of primary brain tumor, and the presence of glioma stem cells (GSCs) has been linked to its resistance to treatments and recurrence. Additionally, aberrant glycosylation has been implicated in the aggressiveness of cancers. However, the influence and underlying mechanism of N-glycosylation on the GSC phenotype and GBM malignancy remain elusive.

pmc-11442824.title: LncRNA PVT1 induces mitochondrial dysfunction of podocytes via TRIM56 in diabetic kidney disease
pmc-11442824.creator: Zhimei Lv, Ziyang Wang, Jinxiu Hu, Hong Su, Bing Liu, Yating Lang, Qun Yu, Yue Liu, Xiaoting Fan, Meilin Yang, Ning Shen, Dongdong Zhang, Xia Zhang, Rong Wang
pmc-11442824.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Mitochondrial dysfunction is a significant contributor to podocyte injury in diabetic kidney disease (DKD). While previous studies have shown that PVT1 might play a vital role in DKD, the precise molecular mechanisms are largely unknown. By analyzing the plasma and kidney tissues of DKD patients, we observed a significant upregulation of PVT1 expression, which exhibited a positive correlation with albumin/creatinine ratios and serum creatinine levels.

pmc-11550349.title: Modelling the factors associated with quality of life in women with osteoporosis: A cross-sectional study
pmc-11550349.creator: Rahmatollah Moradzadeh, Maryam Zamanian, Maliheh Taheri
pmc-11550349.description: BackgroundConsidering the important factors contributing to different health-related quality of life (HRQoL) subscales is essential for implementing preventive measures to increase the HRQoL among women with osteoporosis. We here evaluated the variables related to the mental and physical HRQoL in a sample of Iranian osteoporotic women.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, the participants included 111 women with osteoporosis in 2013.

pmc-11690205.title: AN INTERNATIONAL COLLABORATION TO SUPPORT AGING RESEARCH IN GHANA
pmc-11690205.creator: Tiffany Washington, Dennis Bortey, Fayron Epps, Janelle Gore, Venance Dey
pmc-11690205.description: Nearly 3 million people live with dementia in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). However, ineffective methods for increasing detection and raising awareness contribute to stigma about dementia. By leveraging the resources of universities in developed countries, global community engaged research can increase knowledge and education about dementia in SSA.

pmc-12817757.title: Potassium carbonate as an alternative solution for detecting Anoplocephalid eggs in horse faecal samples
pmc-12817757.creator: Oya Girisgin, Ender Gülegen, Ahmet Onur Girisgin, Veli Yilgor Cirak
pmc-12817757.description: BackgroundAnoplocephalid species are responsible for causing tapeworm infection in horses. The disease may cause serious health issues, including discomfort, colic, and even intestinal perforation and death. A study was carried out to compare the detection rates of tapeworm eggs in naturally infected horses using two different examination solutions.

pmc-13068628.title: Consciousness Disturbances Reported With Clindamycin Versus Cefazolin in Surgical Patients: A Global Pharmacovigilance Analysis Using VigiBase
pmc-13068628.creator: Kazuki Nishida, Basile Chrétien, Hiroshi Morioka, Daigo Tamakoshi, Keita Hiraga, Tomoyuki Nakamura, Shigeyuki Matsui, Masahisa Katsuno, Yoshitaka Hara
pmc-13068628.description: Clindamycin is a common β‐lactam substitute for surgical prophylaxis. Whether peri‐operative disturbances in consciousness are disproportionately reported with clindamycin in global pharmacovigilance data remains unclear. Using WHO VigiBase (up to January 27, 2025), we performed a de‐duplicated case/non‐case disproportionality analysis of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) co‐reporting ≥ 1 anesthetic or sedative.

pmc-13091462.title: Influenza vaccine response is predicted by chronotype and differentially associated with pre- and post-vaccination sleep
pmc-13091462.creator: Elizabeth M. Harrison, Rachel U. Lee, Chad K. Porter, Sandra D. Isidean, Alexandra P. Easterling, Lindsey White, David A. Boulifard, Katherine DeTizio, Zhaodong Liang, Martha Sedegah, Janine Danko, Gena L. Glickman
pmc-13091462.description: Identifying strategies to enhance vaccine response supports public health efforts, particularly in settings where individuals face elevated exposure risks, such as during military deployment or in other high-demand contexts. Accumulating evidence suggests that longer sleep duration may enhance vaccine response, but the role of sleep quality and timing remain less well understood.

pmc-13441777.title: Underlying mechanisms of exercise protection against diabetes mellitus: a narrative review
pmc-13441777.creator: Sizhe Wang, Fan Lu, Yuelin Liu, Ruyi Xu, Guannan Zhang, Yuxin Miao, Shanshan Lu, Zixu Liu, Weiqian Huang, Jinqi Meng, Danyang Tian

uslaw-cfr-t28-s551-4.title: 28 C.F.R. § 551.4 — Hair length.
uslaw-cfr-t28-s551-4.creator: Bureau Of Prisons, Department Of Justice
uslaw-cfr-t28-s551-4.description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 28 (Judicial Administration), Part 551 (Miscellaneous). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). (a) The Warden may not restrict hair length if the inmate keeps it neat and clean. (b) The Warden shall require an inmate with long hair to wear a cap or hair net when working in food service or where long hair could result.

uslaw-cfr-t42-s137-444.title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.444 — If a Self-Governance Tribe objects to the recommended decision, what action will the Secretary take?
uslaw-cfr-t42-s137-444.creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
uslaw-cfr-t42-s137-444.description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). (a) The Secretary has 15 days from the date the Secretary receives timely written objections to modify, adopt, or reverse the recommended decision. If the Secretary does not modify or reverse the recommended decision during that time, the recommended decision automatically becomes final.
